full_judgment:
Siddiqur Rahman Miah J: This is revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure is directed against the judgment and order dated 24-6-1981 rejecting an application for attachment before judgment passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Khulna in the Miscellaneous Case No. 98 of 1981. 

 2. The petitioner Mst Rina Aktar filed miscellaneous Case No. 98 of 1981 in the court of the Subordinate Judge, Khulna for damage. 

 3. The case of the plaintiff petitioner, in short, is that she was given into marriage with the present opposite party, Md Shahidul Islam Mullick, on 26- 9-80 and at the time of marriage, she was given many gold ornaments and other valuables by her parents; that the opposite party was also given a cash of Taka 35,000 on the occasion of the marriage in order to improve his business and that the dower of the present petitioner was fixed at Taka 25,001. It is further stated that the petitioner was divorced by the opposite party on 10-2-1981 on some false and frivolous grounds to misappropriate the petitioner's aforesaid gold ornaments and other valuable property, which led the petitioner to file the suit for damage or recovery of money to the tune of Taka 1,37,201 in the court of Subordinate Judge, Khulna. It is further stated that during pendency of the Miscellaneous case No. 98 of 1981, it was apprehended that the present opposite party would dispose of his shop room No. 162 under the name and style" Fabricks" situated at the KDA New Market, Khulna as soon as he came to know of the institution of the suit for recovery of money. Hence the petitioner filed a petition for attachment of the aforesaid shop room of the opposite party before judgment and the petition was moved before the trial Court who by his order dated 23-4-1981 passed an adinterim order of attachment of the shop with a show cause notice and after filing of the written objection the petition for attachment was heard and ultimately, the learned Subordinate Judge, Khulna by his order No. 41 dated 24-6-1981 rejected the petition vacating the earlier adinterim order for attachment dated 23-4-1981. 

 4. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the order No . 41 dated 24-6-1981 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Khulna in Miscellaneous Case No. 98 of 1981, the petitioner moved this court and obtained the present Rule: 

 6. But the contention of the petitioner as it appears from the record that impugned order No. 41 dated 24-6-1981 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Khulna in Miscellaneous Case No. 98 of 1981 is illegal and arbitrary and the order is liable to be set aside. 

 8. It is contention of the petitioner that she was married with the opposite party No.1 Md Shahidul Islam Mullick on 26-9-1980 and at the time of marriage the opposite party was given some gold ornament and other valuable property by her parents and the opposite party was also given cash of Taka 35,000 on the occasion of the marriage in order to improve his business and the dower of the petitioner was fixed at Taka 25,001 and the petitioner was divorced by the opposite party on 10-2-1981 on some false and frivolous grounds for misappropriating the petitioner's gold ornament and other valuables. It further appears from the record that the petitioner filed Miscellaneous Case No. 98 of 1981 in the court of the learned Subordinate Judge, Khulna for damage and recovery of Taka 1,37,201 on 10-4-1981 along with a petition for permission to sue as pauper. 

 9. During the pendency of the suit, the plaintiff filed an application for attachment before judgment with the contention that the plaintiff is about to transfer his only schedule property. The application was registered as Miscellaneous Case No. 98 of 1981. The defendant, opposite party contested the miscellaneous case by filing written objection contending inter alia that the petition for attachment before judgment is not maintainable in law; that the allegations made in the petition are also vague in nature; that the shop that has been attached before judgment is the only source of livelihood of the opposite party and his brother and that if the same is kept under attachment, the injuries to the brothers of the opposite parties shall surpass the benefit of the petitioner. 

 16. This process is never meant as a lever for the plaintiff to coerce the defendant to come to terms. Hence, utmost caution and circumspection should guide the court. The court must advert to the provision of the Code in this regard, advert to and investigate the allegations thrown against the defendant, satisfy itself that a case for attachment before judgment has been made out and then pass the requisite order. These principles have come to be recognised as mandates to the court and if the courts act in the breach thereof, such an order of the court will have to be ignored as the result of dereliction of duty. 

 18.We find support of the above principles of law in the decision of our apex court reported in the case of Unimarine SA Panama vs Bangladesh 31 DLR (AD) 112. 

 19. In the light of the above mentioned provisions of law, let us now see whether the petitioner has succeeded in proving the prima facie case for getting reliefs for attachment before judgment by affidavit or otherwise. 

 21. The opposite party No. 1 has denied the material allegations and, such allegations have no value unless these are proved by credible evidence. The material evidence on record has even failed to prove the prima facie case of the petitioner. 

 24. In the instant case, none of the requirements could be fulfilled by the petitioner in asking for attachment before judgment. The trial Court having not been satisfied from the material correctly rejected the petition for attachment. In view of what has been stated above, the impugned order dated 24- 6-1981 is sustainable in law.
